questions.question:
A retailer offers the following discount schemes for buyers on an article. Which scheme will be least beneficial to the customer?

i. A discount of 30%.

ii. A discount of 22% followed by a discount of 8%.

iii. Successive discounts of 25% and 5%.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount schemes:

i. A discount of 30%

ii. A discount of 22% followed by a discount of 8%

iii. Successive discounts of 25% and 5%

**Formula used:**

Effective discount for successive discounts = 100 - [(100 - d1) × (100 - d2) / 100]

Where d1 and d2 are the successive discounts.

**Calculation:**

**Scheme i:**

Single discount = 30%

**Scheme ii:**

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - [(100 - 22) × (100 - 8) / 100]

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - [(78 × 92) / 100]

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - 71.76 = 28.24%

**Scheme iii:**

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - [(100 - 25) × (100 - 5) / 100]

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - [(75 × 95) / 100]

⇒ Effective discount = 100 - 71.25 = 28.75%

**Comparison:**

Scheme i = 30%

Scheme ii = 28.24%

Scheme iii = 28.75%

**∴ The least beneficial scheme for the customer is Scheme ii.**

questions.question: The diameter of a hollow hemisphere is 30 cm. Water is filled in it up to its brim. When spherical lead shots each of radius 0.75 cm are dropped into the hemisphere, two-fifth of the water flows out. How many lead shots were dropped into the hemisphere?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the hollow hemisphere (R) = 30 / 2 = 15 cm

Radius of each lead shot (r) = 0.75 cm

Two-fifth of the water flows out

**Formula used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

Number of lead shots = (Volume of water displaced) / (Volume of 1 lead shot)

**Calculations:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

⇒ Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × (15)³

Water displaced = (2/5) × Volume of hemisphere

⇒ Water displaced = (2/5) × (2/3) × π × (15)3

Volume of 1 lead shot = (4/3) × π × r³

⇒ Volume of 1 lead shot = (4/3) × π × (0.75)³

Number of lead shots = Water displaced / Volume of 1 lead shot

⇒ Number of lead shots = [(2/5) × (2/3) × π × (15)3] / [(4/3) × π × (0.75)3]

⇒ Number of lead shots = 1/5 × (15 / 0.75)³ = 1/5 × (20)³ = 1600

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radii of the bases of two cylinders are in the ratio 4:3.

The heights of the two cylinders are in the ratio 9:8.

Ratio of CSA = (r₁ × h₁) : (r₂ × h₂)

**Calculation:**

Let the radii be 4x and 3x, and heights be 9y and 8y respectively.

CSA ratio = (2π × 4x × 9y) : (2π × 3x × 8y)

⇒ CSA ratio = (4 × 9) : (3 × 8)

⇒ CSA ratio = 36 : 24

⇒ CSA ratio = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

Selling price at 10% profit = 110% of CP = ₹20

Desired selling price at 30% profit = 130% of CP

Required increase in selling price = 130% − 110% = 20% of CP

Increase = (20 ÷ 110) × 20 = 400 ÷ 110 = 40 ÷ 11 ≈ ₹3.64

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3.64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹20

Initial Profit₁ = 10%

Required Profit₂ = 30%

**Formula Used:**

CP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dfbaf9d50d1c8611216a9d299e29a65cac92471f357055c5434dd078e2b5359a.png]

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = (200 ÷ 11) × (130 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP₂ = 260 ÷ 11

⇒ Increase in SP = SP₂ − SP₁

⇒ Increase in SP = (260 ÷ 11) − 20

⇒ Increase in SP = (260 − 220) ÷ 11 = 40 ÷ 11

⇒ Increase in SP = 3.6363... ≈ ₹3.64

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

Profit occurs when SP is greater than CP. Profit percentage is always calculated on the CP unless otherwise stated. Formula: Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Marked Price (MP) & Discount

Discount is always offered on the MP. Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount. Formula: Discount% = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Direct Multiplication Factor

questions.question: Several biological processes are catalysed by enzymes. Digestive enzymes are present in which part of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are small organelles found in eukaryotic cells, often referred to as the cell's **"digestive system."**
 
• They contain a variety of **digestive enzymes**, such as proteases, lipases, and nucleases, which help in breaking down macromolecules like **proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids.**
 
• The digestive enzymes within lysosomes function optimally at an **acidic pH**, which is maintained by proton pumps located in the lysosomal membrane.
 
• The primary role of lysosomes is to **degrade cellular waste** and recycle cellular components through processes like **autophagy** (self-eating) and **endocytosis** (engulfing materials from outside the cell).
 
• The enzymes in lysosomes are synthesized in the **rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER)** and are transported to lysosomes via the **Golgi apparatus.**
 
• **Lysosomal dysfunction** can lead to various diseases, such as **Tay-Sachs disease** and **Gaucher's disease**, which are caused by the accumulation of undigested substances.
 
• Lysosomes are often termed as **"suicidal bags"** of the cell because they release enzymes that can digest the cell itself when it is damaged or no longer functional.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ribosome**__

 __
 
• **Ribosomes** are responsible for **protein synthesis** in the cell.
 
• They are composed of **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and proteins.
 
• Ribosomes can be found either **free-floating** in the cytoplasm or attached to the **rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER).**
 
• Unlike lysosomes, ribosomes do not contain digestive enzymes.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Complex**__
 __
 
• The **Golgi complex** is responsible for **modifying, packaging, and transporting proteins and lipids.**
 
• It plays a crucial role in the formation of **lysosomes** by packaging enzymes into vesicles.
 
• It does not directly participate in digestion but aids in the transport of enzymes to lysosomes.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**__
 
 
• **Mitochondria** are known as the **"powerhouses"** of the cell.
 
• They are responsible for generating **ATP** (adenosine triphosphate) through the process of **cellular respiration.**
 
• They do not contain digestive enzymes and are not involved in cellular digestion.
